title: One Scan is Enough: Demonstration-Free Adaptation for Language-Guided Navigation
claim: A single brief scan is compiled into training episodes and policy adaptation, yielding a robot that follows language instructions reliably in real scenes.
layout: 2 panels: 4-step vertical pipeline left, rollout filmstrip rows right, headline stats banner
description: The figure has two halves split by a dashed vertical line. On the left, four numbered blue circles mark a top-to-bottom pipeline joined by curved arrows. Step 1, Scene Scan, is a cartoon of a hand holding an iPhone that scans a living room, with a heat-map overlay on the phone screen. Step 2, Scan2Instruction, shows the reconstructed room beside a top-down floor plan with a dashed path from a green start to a red goal. Step 3, PRPT-KS Post-training, is a small vector diagram with progress, safety and stop axes. It also shows chips for each term and a planner-action arrow that sits above the model-action arrow. Step 4, RealNav Deployment, shows a quadruped robot hearing the speech bubble 'Go to the refrigerator in the kitchen.' On the right, five pastel-tinted rows each show six real-robot camera frames. Each row has a bracketed instruction type, such as Route Following, Human demand or Object Goal, plus the instruction text. A green banner at the bottom reports 85% real-robot success, 2X over other navigation VLAs and 82% unseen-region success, with the numbers in large red text.
caption: One iPhone scan, a deployable language-guided navigation policy. Left: Scan2Instruction compiles a brief handheld scan into scene-specific training episodes, and PRPT-KS adapts RealNav on them with no demonstrations and no human labels. Right: real-robot rollouts following natural-language instructions in the scanned scenes.
abstract: Deploying a language-guided navigation policy in a new building usually means watching it fail. Public-benchmark VLAs degrade scene by scene as layout, appearance, and language drift, and the standard fix of teleoperating fresh trajectories on site does not scale. We replace human demonstration with a single brief iPhone scan. Scan2Instruction compiles that scan into a complete training environment, automatically synthesizing executable navigation episodes with grounded instructions. PRPT-KS then adapts the policy through a closed-form Pareto utility read directly off the reconstructed scene, with no learned critic and no human labels. Across five real environments, the two designs together drive our RealNav to an 85% real-robot success rate, compared with 49% for a RealNav baseline post-trained on human demonstrations, and still achieve 82% in unscanned regions of the same buildings, compared with 41% for the same baseline. Our work turns demonstration-free scene adaptation for language-guided navigation from an aspiration into a working reality.
